literal: pull up the sprouts to help them grow
source: 《孟子·公孙丑上》 (public domain), retold in our own words.
cover: He helped them grow…\Nand killed them all.
hook: He helped them grow…\Nand killed them ALL.
story: Ancient China, state of Song, about 2,300 years ago. An impatient farmer thinks his young rice plants are growing far too slowly. One day he has an idea: he wades into his field and pulls every single seedling up a little, so they look taller. He comes home exhausted but proud and tells his son: 'I helped the plants grow today!' His son runs out to the field and finds every plant wilted and dried up, because their roots were torn loose.
continuity: - THE FARMER: lean man about 45, sunburnt face, thin goatee, impatient frown, wide conical straw hat, patched moss-green tunic, rolled-up brown trousers, muddy bare feet.
- THE SON (only in I5, I6, I7 and, in modern clothes, I9): boy about 12, round face, black hair in two small buns, short ochre tunic, bare feet.
- THE FIELD: one small rice paddy with neat rows of young bright-green rice seedlings standing in shallow water, mud ridges between the rows, a small thatched farmhouse at the edge.
- SETTING: green countryside with soft grey ink-wash hills in the distance, early morning light.
scenes: The twist (used as the hook, first frame of the video)

Medium shot, both faces clear. The farmer stands in his field among rows of rice seedlings that are all wilted, yellow and drooping. He stares at them, jaw dropped, hat slipping off. Next to him his son holds up one limp seedling with a broken root, looking at his father in disbelief. This is the most important image; the editor will push in on it.

The farmer crouches at the edge of his paddy with his arms crossed, glaring at the short green seedlings, tapping one muddy foot impatiently, a frown and a little grumpy cloud of steam above his head. (Only the farmer.)
The farmer suddenly jumps up with a huge, excited grin, one finger raised, eyes shining: he has had a 'brilliant' idea. Behind him, the short seedlings in the paddy. (Only the farmer.)

Wide shot: the farmer, knee-deep in the paddy, bends over and pulls a seedling up a little with both hands; behind him, a long row of seedlings now stands taller and wobbly, their pale roots showing above the water. Sweat drops fly. (Only the farmer.)
Evening at the thatched farmhouse door: the farmer slumps, exhausted, muddy to the knees, but grins proudly and points back toward the field. His son looks up at him curiously.
The son runs barefoot along a mud ridge toward the field, worried, his hair buns bouncing. In the distance the field already looks pale and droopy.
Close-ish shot: the son kneels at the edge of the paddy, shocked, looking at row after row of wilted, yellow, dead seedlings lying flat on the water. Big shocked eyes, hands on his cheeks.
The dead seedlings (background for the big title)

Low close-up of the paddy water: a few limp, yellowed seedlings with their pale roots pulled out of the mud lie in the lower half of the frame. The upper half is calm, plain misty sky with soft grey ink washes and almost nothing in it (we place the big title there). No people.

A small modern living room: the same FARMER (sunburnt face, thin goatee) as a modern dad in a moss-green sweater stacks a tall, wobbly pile of plain books (no titles, no writing) onto a desk in front of the same SON (round face, two hair buns) in a modern ochre T-shirt, who slumps over the desk, exhausted, with dark circles under his eyes. A clock-shaped wall decoration with no numbers. No text, no screens.
lines: He helped every plant grow, and killed them all.
A farmer thought his rice grew way too slowly.
He pulled every seedling up, just a little.
Exhausted but proud: I helped them grow!
His son ran out to see.
Every single plant had dried up.
Pull up the sprouts to help them grow.
It means ruining something by rushing it.
Like pushing a kid into ten classes a day.
title: He pulled up every plant to help it grow… 🌱 | 拔苗助长
desc: 拔苗助长 (bá miáo zhù zhǎng) = ruining something by rushing it. Ever done that? 👇
pinned: 拔 pull · 苗 sprouts · 助 help · 长 grow. 📝 学语言要慢慢来，别拔苗助长。(Xué yǔyán yào mànmàn lái, bié bá miáo zhù zhǎng.) = Learning a language takes time. Don't pull up the sprouts to help them grow.
